course_name_original: Computación Numérica en Ingeniería de Datos

learning_outcomes.text: Know the appropriate mathematical concepts and methods to obtain models capable of solving problems that may arise in the context of data science and engineering: linear algebra, differential and integral calculus.
Evaluate the computational complexity of a problem and identify, if they exist, appropriate algorithmic strategies for its resolution.
Identify the limitations of common algebraic methods when applied to large sparse or structured matrices.
Know efficient methods for solving linear systems and for calculating the singular value decomposition of problems with large matrices.
Solve systems of non-linear equations, using the most appropriate method.
Identify and solve the multivariable interpolation problem.
Interpret and apply various methods of multivariable numerical integration.
Understand the numerical and discretization formulations of Fourier transform and finite differences problems.
Use software tools based on some of the studied methods and also use them as support tools for self-developed programs.

syllabus_topics: Linear Algebra Methods for massive data matrices. Methods for structured matrices.
Solutions of nonlinear equation systems. Multivariable interpolation.
Introduction to the finite difference method.
teaching_methods: Virtual expository sessions with videos, presentations, instructional texts, and self-assessment questionnaires
In-person expository classes to resolve doubts and develop theoretical results with examples
Laboratory practices (virtual and in-person) using MatLab
Tutoring via Teams chat, Virtual Campus forums, or individual/group virtual/in-person tutorials

assessment_methods.method: Project report (individual theoretical study and Matlab implementation)
Attendance and participation in in-person activities

assessment_rules: For ordinary call, the final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.2 MP + 0.5 NEx + 0.15 NA + 0.15 NCv, where MP is project report, NEx is exam grade, NA is attendance and classroom work, and NCv is Virtual Campus tasks. For differentiated evaluation, NA is replaced by NT (mandatory tutoring attendance and work). For extraordinary calls, there will be two exams, one on theoretical-practical content and one on programming methods with Matlab, each weighing 50% of the final grade.
